P1.evidence: The strongest open in the batch. Setter notes were genuinely read back with specifics, not just referenced: 'I spoke with Kim, so he just briefed me in on your situation' followed by 'Kim mentioned that you've been training a few times a week. You've got the kettlebells at home, correct?' Frame agreement was asked and given — 'Yeah? Sounds good?' / 'Sure, sounds good.' The open question was clean and two-pronged: 'Where are you actually right now, and what's the main thing you're trying to change?' The frame itself was three-part rather than four — situation, goals, how we build it around you, plus a no-hard-feelings exit — with no explicit what's-in-the-way element, so P1b scores partial.

P2.evidence: Six of nine run properly and several of them better than the script asks for. Sleep was not just asked but probed for consistency: 'you can sleep seven hours every single night, but if one day you go to sleep at 11 p.m., another day you go, I don't know, two in the morning.' Energy was asked with a scale and then followed up for pattern. Diet was pushed past the easy answer — 'When you say balanced, do you mean like whole foods or do you eat also like processed food too? And be honest, please' — which produced the bread, alcohol and processed-food admissions. Injuries were asked twice, including for history, and then extended into a sitting-related stiffness probe that surfaced the straddle-fold limitation. The two misses matter though: age, height and weight were never established at any point, and health conditions were never asked, which is why a suspected SIBO diagnosis only surfaced by accident thirty-four minutes in.

P3.evidence: The deep-why work genuinely landed and the prospect said so: 'It wasn't clear to me until now' and 'I mean, it was clear, but I think that this made it way more specific than before.' The bridge was direct — 'why do you want to do that' — and the forward projection was a strong variant of the script: 'when you think about yourself, like in six months, when you actually finished the transformation with Trevor... what becomes possible?' That produced emotional regulation, confidence in meetings and assertive communication, which the rep then reflected back and locked in as 'the beast in the meeting room'. Marked down on three counts: nobody else's stake was ever explored — no partner, no family, no colleagues — so P3f is a clean miss and P3g only reached identity and work, not relationships or legacy; nothing physical he wants to do but cannot was surfaced; and the rep spent a substantial stretch of this phase answering his own question, narrating his hiking why and retelling a story about a sixty-year-old wealth-management client.

P4.evidence: Clean. Past attempts were opened on the prospect's own reference point and worked forward — the 2016 CrossFit summer, what it produced, then the direct question 'what was the main reason you fell off of the wagon afterwards?' The prospect took it seriously ('That's a really good question') and produced a real answer about substituting running without planning it. The structural gap was surfaced by the rep's clarifying question rather than volunteered: 'when you say be clear on what you do, like you mean that you need a structure to the process of what to do in the workout?' — which is what made the prospect articulate 'to not spend that much time thinking what routine should I do'. The present-tense blocker was never asked directly, and the 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' line was not used.

P5.evidence: Not attempted. No two-year question, no test of willingness to settle, no why-not, no line in the sand. The rep ran the mirror image instead — a positive future-pace about what becomes possible in six months — which builds desire but creates no cost of inaction. This is the third consecutive sales call in this batch where phase 5 is entirely absent, and here it is the decisive one: a prospect with no downside pressure and a functioning cheaper substitute has nothing to weigh $6,000 against.

P6.evidence: Textbook, and correctly placed before the price. Belief was tested with the goal tied in: 'If you had this right training, simple nutrition, and accountability from Trevor built around your lifestyle, would you agree that you would get to your goals and be the beast in the meeting room?' / 'Yeah, I agree.' The all-in check followed immediately and in the scripted form: 'If we can figure out all the details, are you fully committed to showing up and doing the work to become that version 2.0 of Antonio?' / 'I am.' The rep also caught an earlier micro-hesitation and named it — 'You hesitated for a second' — which is good practice. P6c is partial because when that hesitation surfaced the rep did not return to phase 5, he reframed forward to commitment; and because phase 5 did not exist on this call there was nowhere to return to.

P11.evidence: The close was attempted — price presented, commitment obtained beforehand — but the offer was refused, so payment and everything downstream of it were unreachable. N/A rather than miss, per the rule that a phase the call could not reach drops out of the denominator. Worth noting the prospect had a hard stop and was being texted into a meeting while the money conversation was still live, so even the objection sequence was truncated by the clock.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran twice and ran well — 'Let me be frank. Like, finances aside... Apart from that, there is anything else that would be keeping you from being less than 100% sure that you want to do this' and then, after the CrossFit comparison, 'apart from the finances, let's put the finances aside. Would you like to do it, still?' followed by 'if you had the money, you would do it... There's nothing else, no hesitation about it.' That is the cleanest isolation in the batch. The break-it-up move started — 'most guys just pay it up front. But for some people, we can make an exception and talk about how we could break it up to make it more digestible' — and was then abandoned. Not one item of the financial picture was collected: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments, despite the prospect having volunteered that he has 'investments I have going on' which is precisely the thread the script tells you to pull. The prospect's meeting cut it short, but the rep had already spent his last five minutes without asking a single financial question.

This is the documented script gap firing exactly as predicted — a cheaper alternative that genuinely worked. CrossFit is not a hypothetical substitute for this prospect: it produced what he calls the fittest period of his life, and he priced it at a quarter of the offer for the same six months. Objection C has no branch for this because it assumes the blocker is capacity to pay rather than value against a functioning low-cost option. The rep improvised a one-time-cost-versus-recurring reframe — 'you're learning this for life. So you won't need any other CrossFit memberships anymore, so you pay it once, and you're good for life' — which is a reasonable instinct and did not move him ('Yeah, no, I understand that'). The stronger unused line was sitting in the transcript: he had already told the rep he abandoned CrossFit in New York because it was too expensive and too far away, so the substitute has a documented failure record with this exact buyer.

Second script gap, and a new one: a currency and purchasing-power objection. 'It's high for like when you change it to Mexican currency' and 'this is probably like a better fit for people in the UK... for Mexican currency, I think I would have better options that better fit my current needs.' There is no play for a prospect who accepts the value, accepts the fit, and rejects the price on regional purchasing power. The rep did not acknowledge it at all — he answered the CrossFit comparison and let the geography argument stand unchallenged. The stated ICP contains no geographic or purchasing-power criterion, so nothing upstream screened for this either.

Third gap, this one clinical rather than commercial: the prospect disclosed a suspected SIBO diagnosis under active investigation with gastroenterologists and nutritionists, and tied it directly to the nutrition protocol being sold. There is no scripted handling for a prospect with an open GI investigation. The rep did not ask what the clinicians had said, did not qualify the protocol, and pivoted to a personal anecdote about his own snacking.

notes: Score this one high and lose it — that is the correct outcome and the corpus needs cases like it. Open, baseline, past attempts, root cause and the commitment check were all run properly, and the commitment check was in the right place for once, which produced an unhesitating yes before any number was spoken. Two things cost the deal and only one of them is coachable. The coachable one: no consequence frame, again. A prospect who is not in pain, has a gym membership he barely uses and a cheaper option that once worked has nothing pressing against him at the moment of decision, and phase 5 is the only part of the process that manufactures that pressure. The uncoachable one is a genuine business finding rather than a rep failure — the offer is priced in a currency this buyer converts at, he said so plainly, and neither the script nor the ICP has anything to say about it. Third point for the coach: he asked in the middle of the objection for 'a pre-recorded workout or something like that to be more cost-efficient', which is a product the company sells for $200 a month, and the rep held it back for a phone call the next day instead of putting it in front of a buyer who was asking for it by name.
